memory_update.text: DPZ should remain the reference benchmark for restaurant franchisor-owned supply-chain economics: vertically integrated dough / ingredient manufacturing and distribution can be compared against smaller chains and suppliers.

FARM enters the speculative-shadow lane as a micro-cap foodservice beverage / DSD supplier; survival in later layers requires primary-source confirmation of restaurant-chain customer exposure and margin recovery.
WEST enters the underfollowed lane as a B2B coffee / tea / extract platform that may function as outsourced beverage commissary infrastructure for foodservice operators.

THS enters the underfollowed lane as a scaled private-label manufacturer with possible outsourced foodservice manufacturing relevance, especially after acquiring Farmer Brothers' Northlake and non-DSD assets.
Need primary SEC filing checks for FARM, WEST, and THS before treating them as true restaurant supply-chain chokepoint names; current evidence establishes plausibility, not material exposure.

node: Franchise-owned or franchisor-controlled commissary, ingredient manufacturing, and distribution networks
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the restaurant commissary / captive supply-chain node. Domino's is the reference case because its vertically integrated dough manufacturing and food distribution network appears to support franchisee economics and system growth. The underfollowed discovery lane shifts away from restaurant brands and toward B2B foodservice input suppliers, private-label beverage/coffee processors, DSD networks, and ingredient manufacturing assets that may benefit from chain standardization, franchisor procurement scale, and outsourcing of centralized food production. Evidence is strongest for DPZ as the reference model and weaker but plausible for FARM, WEST, and THS as second-order suppliers or infrastructure beneficiaries.
